bullets: VyADrwRPJz8 game 7 (t=1273-1538), the last game of a #1-ladder-push session, against a Giant Skeleton / Hero Balloon beatdown deck with Wizard, Electro Wizard, Barbarians and Log/Fireball/Tornado. Goes to overtime; no tower falls inside the readable window (own right 252, enemy right ~281, enemy left 1229 at the end), so the result is unrecorded.

The list runs two cheap win conditions and nothing else offensive: Goblin Barrel on tower corners (clock 2:24, 1:57, 0:59, 0:47, 0:22, OT 1:41, OT 1:29, OT 0:49, OT 0:40) and Wall Breakers at the bridge in whichever lane the opponent just spent elixir in (clock 2:28 split, 2:04, 1:22, 0:58, 0:12, OT 1:40, OT 0:55, OT 0:31). Damage comes from repetition, not from any single big push.

Defence is Bomb Tower plus a 1-elixir spirit, with Royal Delivery held back for the opponent's support: "Let's berserker here on defense. We have the delivery ready in case he goes for an e-wiz" (clock 1:15). The Bomb Tower is cycled five times in 264 s and once placed at the bridge ([11, 13], OT 1:50) purely to pull the Balloon backwards.

Magic Archer is the deck's swing card and is played three different ways: pre-emptive anti-air with a delayed Ice Spirit (clock 1:44), deliberately deep when the bridge is unsafe ("I want to marcher the bridge, but I know it's not worth it. Let's just go for a low marcher", clock 0:35), and as a piercing chip finisher hunting an arrow line at the bridge in overtime (OT 0:35).

Stated weakness of the list in this matchup: splash support. "Evo wizard is the card that I'm super scared of, guys, cuz I really can't deal with the evo wizard good at all" (clock 0:45), and the game is decided on his right tower once the Balloon connects twice — "Please don't get two. Oh my god, that got two. That is the worst possible situation" (OT 0:57).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Berserker and the two spirits all want the opponent's small spell, and Ryley plays them explicitly to drain it ("Force out the log again. Oh, force out the e-wiz").
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two 2-3 elixir win conditions that both die to the same cards mean the opponent's Log, Zap or Barbarian Barrel is never in hand when it is needed: Ryley cycles Goblin Barrel on the tower corners and Wall Breakers at the bridge, alternating lanes so each threat lands into a spent answer. The four-card defensive core is deliberately cheap and reusable — Bomb Tower for ground, Royal Delivery held for Electro Wizard, Minion Horde or a Balloon, and Ice Spirit / Fire Spirit both as the last layer of a defence and as follow-ups on a barrel. Magic Archer is the only card above 3 elixir besides the Bomb Tower and does the work the swarm-less list cannot otherwise do: air defence, swarm clearing and piercing chip from a safe tile. The obvious hole is heavy splash support — against a Wizard he says outright he "can't deal with the evo wizard good at all" — so the plan is to out-tempo it rather than to answer it.
